verdict: Bengaluru's froth picture ticks slightly hotter vs early-July: inventory overhang has stretched from ~12 to ~15 months as Q2 2026 launches came in +41% YoY (to ~21,670 units) while absorption failed to keep pace, moving that indicator from green to amber. Balance-sheet risk remains benign — RBI's June 2026 FSR pins housing GNPA at just 0.5% (down from ~1.0% at prior read) and system GNPA at a multi-decade low of 1.8% — and RBI held repo at 5.25% at the June MPC with the next decision on Aug 3–5. Two-speed market persists: banks and borrowers healthy, but ~96% of Q2 launches priced ≥₹80L and Indiranagar asking prices 50–80% over guidance keep the luxury-concentration froth flag flying.

indicators.name: Unsold inventory overhang
indicators.value: Bengaluru ~15 months (up from ~12); pan-India Q2 2026 unsold ~6.16 lakh units
indicators.note: Bengaluru overhang stretched from ~12 months to ~15 months as Q2 2026 launches surged +41% YoY to ~21,670 units and absorption lagged. Bengaluru unsold stock closed 2025 at ~64,900 units (+23% YoY) with 2026 projected near ~70,000. Shift from expansion to stabilization, not distress.
indicators.src: Anarock / Meraqi / Business Today Q2 2026 residential viewpoints

indicators.name: Launch mix skew to luxury
indicators.note: Q2 2026 saw ~21,670 new units launched (up 41% YoY) with ~96% concentrated in premium/luxury segments (≥₹80L), up from ~68% premium share in Q1. Mid-income and affordable supply continues to be crowded out as builders bet on IT/startup high-income buyers.
indicators.src: NewsFirst Prime citing Anarock Q2 2026 launch data

indicators.name: EMI-to-income (affordability)
indicators.value: EMI/income 35% H1 2026 vs 34% H2 2025; repo held at 5.25%
indicators.note: Knight Frank Affordability Index H1 2026: Bengaluru's EMI-to-income ratio worsened marginally from 34% to 35% — still comfortably below the 50% stress line but the cushion is eroding. RBI held repo at 5.25% at its June 2026 MPC (unanimous, neutral stance); next meeting Aug 3–5, 2026. Typical home-loan rates 7.9–8.4%.
indicators.src: Knight Frank India Affordability Index H1 2026; RBI MPC June 2026

indicators.name: Housing-loan defaults (NPAs)
indicators.note: RBI Financial Stability Report June 2026: housing-loan GNPA at just 0.5% (down from ~1.0% prior read; historical ~1.2% in 2019). System GNPA at multi-decade low of 1.8%, projected to edge to 1.9% by FY28. However, loans ≥₹50L now make up 44.7% of outstanding housing credit, and household debt at 45.5% of GDP is on RBI's watchlist.

indicators.name: Asking vs registered price gap
indicators.note: Indiranagar guidance ~₹12k/sqft vs market ₹18–22k/sqft (50–80% premium). Newer corridors (Devanahalli, Hoskote) narrower at 15–25%. Feb 2026 6–15% guidance hike (12–15% Devanahalli/Yelahanka/Hebbal) plus Aug 2025 doubling of registration fee (1%→2%) partially closed the gap but froth persists in prime pockets. Total statutory outlay ~7.5–7.6% on flats >₹45L — among India's highest.
indicators.src: Squareyards Bangalore rates; OneCity guidance-value tracker

indicators.name: Registration volumes
indicators.value: No fresh June 2026 aggregate; Kaveri 2.0 digital upgrade live
indicators.note: Karnataka Stamp (Digital e-Stamp) Rules operationalised Jan 2026; Kaveri 2.0 upgrade progressing. Registration fee doubled to 2% (Aug 2025) + Feb 2026 guidance hike likely dampened Q1–Q2 2026 transaction counts, but no June 2026 aggregate stamp-duty collection figure was publicly reported. Buyer-cost headwinds continue.
